=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Location: per-file blob comparison, the existing `elif` chain at the lines touched by the last-run diff (the `elif [ -n "${phase7_base_blob}" ] && [ "${phase7_base_blob}" != "${phase7_merge_base_blob}" ]` branch).
  Issue: Symmetry gap — when the *base* contents API (`gh api repos/.../contents/${path}?ref=${PHASE7_BASE_REF}`) fails for a given file, `phase7_base_blob` ends up empty and the existing condition `[ -n "${phase7_base_blob}" ]` evaluates false. The branch then falls through to the `else` clause and emits `outcome=kept reason=base_unchanged_since_merge_base`, which is misleading: we never verified whether the base actually changed since the merge base, we simply couldn't read it.
  Suggested minimal fix: add one more `elif` ahead of the existing comparison, parallel to the just-added branch:
  `elif [ -z "${phase7_base_blob}" ]; then`
  `  echo "PHASE7_UNCONFLICT_FILE path=${phase7_path} outcome=kept reason=base_blob_unavailable"`
  Pin it in `tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_phase7_unconflict.py::test_unconflict_only_rewrites_files_the_base_changed_since_merge_base` with the same `elif`/reason strings already used for the merge-base failure. Net change ~4 lines.
  Runtime impact: when the base contents API fails for a single file in a conflicted set, the operator log carries an accurate reason (`base_blob_unavailable`) instead of an incorrect one, and the eventual `still_conflicted` retry outcome becomes diagnosable without re-running the workflow. The gate's pass/fail decision is unchanged — both branches skip the rewrite and leave the conflict for the retry attempt to resolve (or not). No API call shape changes.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: 3490-3494 (the `else` branch of the per-file condition chain)
  Problem: When the base contents API call at line 3479 fails, `phase7_base_blob` is empty. The condition at line 3490 (`[ -n "${phase7_base_blob}" ] && ...`) short-circuits to false, so the `else` branch at line 3492-3493 logs `outcome=kept reason=base_unchanged_since_merge_base`. This mislabels an API failure as "base unchanged since merge base" — the base blob was unavailable, not confirmed equal to the merge-base blob.
  Why it fails at runtime: An operator debugging a future `no_run` failure would see `base_unchanged_since_merge_base` in the log and conclude the base did not touch the file, when in reality the base contents lookup failed and the file was kept as a fail-closed default. The safe action (keep the PR version) is taken either way, so there is no runtime correctness impact — only diagnostic accuracy.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
